question: Should OpenClaw core support direct cross-gateway session messaging now, or keep this in plugins/bridges until a federation and security contract is approved?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the implementation expands gateway trust boundaries, session ownership, message delivery, and config surface, so automation cannot choose the durable product/security contract.

options.title: Design core contract first
options.body: Define the gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility contract before landing a core implementation.

options.title: Plugin or MCP bridge first
options.body: Keep core gateway-local and expose only missing plugin/API seams needed for external bridges to implement cross-gateway routing safely.

options.title: Wait for federation FRD
options.body: Hold the concrete sessions feature behind #87733 until maintainers settle bridge transport and tenant-scoped operator policy.

recommendation.title: Design core contract first
recommendation.body: Define the gateway-to-gateway identity, authorization, replay/idempotency, and session-visibility contract before landing a core implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The history trail for session-tool architecture, gatewayUrl security, and session resolution points to steipete as the strongest decision owner.
